title: Plum Clafoutis with Orange
summary: Plum halves soaked in orange and baked in a creamy almond batter until caramelised at the edges and barely set in the middle.
equipment: 23 cm round or oval baking dish (about 2 litres)

ingredients.item: soft unsalted butter, for the dish
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Macerate the plums
steps.text: Toss the plums with 40 g sugar, the orange zest and juice and leave 20 minutes while the oven heats to 165 °C (145 °C fan). The sugar and citrus soften the plum skins and draw out some juice for the batter.

steps.title: Prepare the dish
steps.text: Butter the dish and arrange the plums in it cut side up, pouring any juice over them.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the 100 g sugar until smooth, then add the flour, ground almonds and salt. Whisk in the cream and vanilla to a smooth, pourable batter.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Pour the batter around the plums and bake 55-65 minutes, until golden, set at the edges and only barely trembling in the middle (71 °C). The low oven keeps this rich, creamy batter custardy rather than rubbery.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Sprinkle with the remaining sugar while hot and let stand 15 minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Choose ripe but firm plums so the halves hold their shape.
A common mistake is baking it in a hot oven, which makes this creamy batter rubbery.
Swap in apricots or nectarines when plums are out of season.
Sprinkling sugar over while hot gives a light sparkly crust.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Serve at room temperature.
